speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe the exact location and nature of your right groin pain, and tell me if you have noticed any abnormal positioning of your leg since the rear-end collision.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Did the pain localize specifically to the front of the right hip over the femoral artery region, or does it extend to the outer hip? Also, are you currently able to move your right leg without it falling inward or outward abnormally?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Femoral Neck Fracture.

Based on the mechanism of injury (rear-end collision), severe right groin pain, and the classic deformity of the right leg being shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated, this clinical picture is pathognomonic for a femoral neck fracture. I am requesting immediate imaging to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Hip_XRay
